title: The tin flute and the cornet from Prechter
summary: He first played a six-hole tin flute; a white man named Prechter gave him an old cornet, which he never mastered.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yeah. Can you tell us about when you first took up music, what your first instrument was, and your teacher, or anyone that you helped you?

Well, I'll tell you. Helped you? When I first started to try to play, I used to play a flute. You know those ten flutes? Oh, yeah. When I was so good on them, everybody tried to encourage me to play music. At that time things were so hard, I mean I never could buy an instrument, you see? But I really could play one of them things. How long were you then? When I was going to school, I must have been around about nine, ten years old.
Was that one of those straight flutes?

The straight ten flutes, yeah, the six hole. And a white fella by the name of Prechter, he happened to find an old cornet laying around his house. After he used to hear me playing that flute all the time, he gave me the cornet. I fooled around with that and played on it and tried to learn a couple of pieces, but I never would call myself a cornet player, you know? I was a little girl. We made up a little band, guitar, I mean at that time they used to be banjos. I was playing the cornet and we had a fella named Lawrence Boynes who was playing clarinet. Lil' Well, he was playing drum. We played around, people used to hire us for little parties. We'd do about five or six pieces, you know? You were all youngsters? All kids, yeah, all kids. So, that went on for a while and around 1917, I decided to join the Navy. Well, I had been gone a little better than a year. And I happened to meet one of John's brothers, which we for his cousins, you know? John Casimir.
